title: NovelBrain
description: The AUTHORED static 'constitution' of a novel (Novel Brain DSL, roadmap P15). It is neither a story fact (ADR-006) nor a recomputed projection (ADR-008: StoryState is a fold; the Brain is not). It is a THIRD artifact class — an authored, near-static input the author writes by hand — so it lives under sources/ (next to sources/manifest.yaml and reference-novels), NEVER under registry/facts/ or registry/derived/. It declares mission, genre, target reader, the reader promise, the writing/forbidden style, commercial position and the intended emotional curve. Every agent and prompt reads it as the single source of intent: its writing_style + forbidden_style feed the chapter-draft prompt's style directive. ADVISORY — validating it (runtime.cli brain check) never gates a build (ADR-003).

mission.description: The one-sentence reason this novel exists — what it is fundamentally trying to do for its reader.

channel.description: e.g. 男频 / 女频 / general

who.description: The reader this novel is written for.

avoids.description: What makes that reader drop a book.

promise.description: The core promise to the reader — the payoff the whole book is contracted to deliver.

voice.description: The narrative voice/tone to write in.

pov.description: Point of view, e.g. 第三人称限知 / first person.

forbidden_style.description: Hard 'never do this' rules — anti-patterns the draft must not exhibit (e.g. 注水, 上帝视角剧透, 主角龟缩).

commercial_position.description: How this book is positioned commercially (optional; complements the Market Snapshot, which is a derived market read).

emotional_curve.description: The intended emotional trajectory across the book (ordered beats). Advisory intent, not a per-chapter schedule.

beat.description: A named emotional beat, e.g. 憋屈 -> 爆发.

at.description: Rough location, e.g. 第一卷末 / 30%.

long_term_theme.description: The through-line theme the whole novel is ultimately about.

reader_expectation.description: Standing expectations the reader will hold the book to (爽点/期待), which prompts and reviewers should honor.
